title: How to fake on an instrument
summary: He explains faking as practice in every key, playing harmony by ear through the chord and weaving around the melody.

story.theme_name: Teaching jazz: schools, students and advice to the young
story.community_name: What to think while improvising: wrong notes and being in the moment

blocks.x: He had been taught solfeggio and music before he ever got to an instrument, see, so after he got the hang of the instrument it was quite easy then. He just learned to coordinate the tool, you see.
Well how does a guy like that learn how to fake? That's something that's always fascinating to me.

Well fake is nothing but practice. People that can't fake have never practiced faking. To learn a fake, you play a tune and you try to play the same tune in a different key and in another different key and keep trying different keys until you can play it in any key practically. And you learn your instrument, you learn the sound of your instrument, that just, subconsciously you just play the thing without even having to think of what you're doing.
Now when the trumpet's carrying the lead how are you going to make up those variations? How does that come?
That gets mostly by ear. You play a third away or a fifth away, the harmony, through the chord, you run through the chord, you know.
Do you think about those chords much yourself?
Well you do at first but now I don't even think of the chords, I just know them.

When I hear the tune I know the chord, I just feel the chord more or less. You could call it a feeling, you know. And you just weave in and out through the chord and all around the melody. You stay away from his note more or less or you'll pass over it going to another one. But you never linger on the same note as the melody unless you want to, you see.
